all_found.desc: [ADVISORY] The doc comment declares MainWorktreeFromPorcelain/RunStoreRoot 'the ONE definition of where FSM runs live', but internal/status/fsmruns.go (DiscoverAbandonedRuns, called from status.go:221 with the current-worktree root) still reads <current worktree>/.metareview/runs, so a third reader of the run store was not moved onto the shared seam. From a linked worktree, `metareview status` (and the Stop hook built on it) still cannot see abandoned FSM runs the FSM wrote to the main worktree. This is the same writer/reader split as #169 on a different surface, and the comment tells future maintainers the split cannot happen.

[ADVISORY] TestRunStoreReadersAreDeclared checks whole files and matches only the exact literal `".metareview", "runs"`. cmd/metareview/main.go already contains `RunStoreRoot(`, so a second current-worktree reader added to main.go passes, and a path spelled differently (".metareview/runs", a constant) is never inspected. The worktree.go doc comment (lines 18-20) claims the test enforces the rule for any reader, which is stronger than what it checks. The #169 regression guard can miss a new reader in main.go, the most likely place for one, and the comment overstates how much protection the test gives.

findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] internal/repo was a stdlib-only leaf used for root detection by about 11 packages, and it now imports internal/fsm/gate just to reach RealExec's GIT_* scrubbing. That pulls fsm/gate, fsm/run, fsm/converge, fsm/errs, state and jsonl into every importer of repo, and makes the root-detection package and the FSM depend on each other through gate. No import cycle exists today. But fsm/run, fsm/gate, state and jsonl can now never import internal/repo without creating one, and every package that uses repo.Root picks up the FSM execution stack. Moving the hardened git exec into a small leaf package that both gate and repo import would avoid this.

findings.consequence: If gitcontext.Deadline is tuned or overridden in tests, this call does not follow it. The FSM (writer) and record-lenses (reader) also reach git through different runners, so they can behave differently on timeout or error even though they parse the same porcelain output.
findings.issue: runStoreGit hardcodes its own 20s timeout and exec path when the repo already has gitcontext.Deadline, the shared git deadline that tests can override. Two git runners now resolve the main worktree: the FSM's c.git runner and this one.

findings.consequence: The #169 regression guard can miss a new reader in main.go, the most likely place for one, and the comment overstates how much protection the test gives.

The worktree.go doc comment (lines 18-20) claims the test enforces the rule for any reader, which is stronger than what it checks.

findings.consequence: If record-lenses runs with GIT_DIR, GIT_COMMON_DIR or GIT_WORK_TREE exported (from a git hook or a wrapper), it can resolve a different main worktree than the FSM wrote to, and the #169 'no such FSM run' failure comes back under those conditions.
findings.issue: RunStoreRoot's comment says it resolves the main worktree 'exactly as the FSM resolves it', but runStoreGit runs `git worktree list --porcelain` with the caller's full environment, while the FSM writer (rootOf via gate.RealExec) strips GIT_* variables (scrubEnv) and sets GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 and LC_ALL=C. The two share the parser but not the git invocation.

Moving the hardened git exec into a small leaf package that both gate and repo import would avoid this.
findings.issue: internal/repo was a stdlib-only leaf used for root detection by about 11 packages, and it now imports internal/fsm/gate just to reach RealExec's GIT_* scrubbing. That pulls fsm/gate, fsm/run, fsm/converge, fsm/errs, state and jsonl into every importer of repo, and makes the root-detection package and the FSM depend on each other through gate.

findings.consequence: The CHANGELOG release date is one day off from the actual release date.
findings.issue: The 0.13.4 entry is dated 2026-09-27, but the release commits are dated 2026-09-26 (-0700), and the previous entry used the local commit date.
